chunks: Abu Nasr Hibatullah ibn Muhammad said:

The tomb of Uthman ibn Sa'id is on the western side of the City is on the western side of Baghdad (the City of Peace), in Maidan Street, at the beginning of the place known as the alley of Jubla, in the alley's mosque to the right of the entrance, and the tomb is in the exact direction of the qibla of the mosque, may God have mercy on him.

key_terms.الدَّرْبِ: The alley or street, referring to a specific thoroughfare.
key_terms.جُبْلَةَ: Jubla, a place or gate name associated with the location.
key_terms.عُثْمَانَ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ: Uthman ibn Sa'id, a prominent companion of the Imams and one of the Four Emissaries.
key_terms.قِبْلَةِ الْمَسْجِدِ: The direction of prayer in the mosque, indicating the tomb's orientation.
key_terms.مَدِينَةِ السَّلَامِ: The City of Peace, a historical name for Baghdad.

ai.seo_question: Where is the tomb of Uthman ibn Sa'id located in Baghdad?
ai.summary: This narration by Abu Nasr Hibatullah ibn Muhammad provides precise topographical details for the tomb of Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Kummi, one of the Four Emissaries (al-Nuwwab al-Arba'ah) of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari during the Minor Occultation. Located in the western sector of Baghdad's city of peace, specifically within the courtyard of the Darb Jabala mosque, this site serves as a key pilgrimage destination (ziyarat) for Shias, anchoring the historical reality of the Imam's hidden presence in the urban landscape of Abbasid Baghdad.
